clue.text: Green spaces highly regarded in urban areas

definitions.text: Green spaces highly regarded in urban areas

parts.words: Green spaces highly regarded in urban areas
parts.note: highly regarded reads literally: city lawns and flowerbeds looked up at because they sit on top of buildings

explanation.surface: Parks are much prized by city dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly regarded' seems to mean admired, but read literally it means gazed up at, high above the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Planted terraces on top of city buildings are green spaces located high up.

clue.text: Stock book

definitions.meaning: a supply kept back for later use
to arrange ahead, as with a table or seat

explanation.definitionFit: A store held back is a stock, and to arrange a table in advance is to book it.

clue.text: The coppers put inside also broke stones

indicators.note: put inside says the coins go within the other letters
broke says the letters of also are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: coppers are small coins, pennies, abbreviated P

explanation.surface: Some police officers went inside and smashed the stones as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' makes OALS from ALSO, and 'put inside' sets P in it. 'Coppers' looks like police officers, but here it means pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gems, and gems are commonly called stones.

clue.text: It's topping for the Highlander!

parts.note: topping means headgear, not something splendid: a Scottish woollen cap worn on top of the head

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's exclamation that something is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' is old British slang for excellent, but here it is what tops the head. A GLENGARRY is a brimless Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: This brimless Scots cap is a hat that tops a Highland outfit.

clue.text: Stern nurse

definitions.meaning: the back end of a ship
to bring up or raise a child

explanation.definitionFit: The back part of a vessel is its stern, and to raise young is to nurse them.

clue.text: Men involved in a row about agreement show sense

indicators.note: about says the crew goes round the word of agreement

parts.note: a rowing eight is the crew of oarsmen pulling together in one boat
yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: Rowdy men argue over a deal and show good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is rowing: the men are a boat crew. 'about' signals that the crew's word wraps around the word of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Skinhead getting on top of goody-goody youth

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on top of another comes before it

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter, S
a prig is a smugly virtuous person

explanation.surface: A thuggish youth bullies a prim young swot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' looks like the shaven-headed youth, but it is the head of 'skin': S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprig is an old, slightly scornful word for a young lad.

clue.text: Unprofessional, but of a mature disposition

indicators.note: disposition, an arrangement, says the letters of a mature are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Not paid for the work, yet of a grown-up temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like character, but it signals a rearranging of A MATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doing a thing for love rather than pay is unprofessional.

clue.text: Breakfast in gaol?

parts.note: a morning oat dish, which in British slang is also a term served in prison

explanation.surface: What prisoners might eat in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, doing PORRIDGE means serving time in prison, so the dish is both the breakfast and the gaol sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats boiled in milk are a breakfast dish, and the same word is British slang for a prison term.

clue.text: Draw the old fellow

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: Sketch the aged man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching, but it is the noun: a game ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a position where no move is possible ends the game as a tie.

clue.text: Girl soldiers standing around a carrier

indicators.note: standing around says the soldiers surround the next piece

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A girl watches troops gathered round a porter.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOD is a builder's tray on a pole for carrying bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name.

clue.text: Some scores ignore their entitlement to leave

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Many people disregard their right to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: to quit a job is everyone's entitlement, read as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a post is something anyone has a right to do, so stepping down is their entitlement to leave.

clue.text: Eject constituents so rigged out

indicators.note: constituents, the parts of something, together with out says these letters are broken up and reformed
rigged out joined with constituents says the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Voters throw out a fixed election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' and 'out' signal rearranging SO RIGGED; the surface pictures voters and a fixed ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew something forth is to throw it out, which is to eject it.

clue.text: Close by a river or brook

parts.note: close as a noun means the end
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Near a river or a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a stream to go with 'river', but it is the verb meaning tolerate. The URE is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate it, to put up with it.

clue.text: Get rid of locks and there'll be trouble!

parts.note: dis is a prefix meaning to remove or undo
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Shave your head and expect problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the word apart as DIS-TRESS gives 'remove hair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is anguish or difficulty, a form of trouble.

clue.text: Ought with little hesitation to assume responsibility

parts.note: should is a near-synonym of ought
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: One must, after a brief pause, take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a burden on one's back is to take on a duty.

clue.text: A French male the cads molested is not hurt

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for a

indicators.note: molested says the letters of the cads are knocked about

explanation.surface: A Frenchman survives a mauling by some rogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'molested' makes SCATHED from THE CADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through without injury means being undamaged.

clue.text: Attacked a fool and suffered for it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ailed means suffered from illness

explanation.surface: Someone set on a fool and paid for it with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set upon violently means being under attack.

clue.text: Bacon maybe to try first

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
1ST abbreviates first, with I standing for the figure one

explanation.surface: Sampling the bacon before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' is Francis Bacon, the English writer of essays, not breakfast meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English writer famous for his short prose pieces.

clue.text: Overwrought, though that's no longer mentioned

parts.note: ex is the prefix for former
cited means mentioned or quoted

explanation.surface: Agitated, though the matter has stopped being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and agitated is being overwrought.

clue.text: Like general quiet when taking a nap

parts.note: as means like
Robert E Lee was the American Confederate general
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A commander is silent when dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an adjective, but it is General Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone napping is sleeping.

clue.text: Protect a wild-plant enclosure

parts.note: to pad is to cushion and so protect
dock is a common broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: Fence off a patch of wild flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fenced field for horses is an enclosure.

clue.text: Many a daring agitator can appear woolly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: agitator says the letters of a daring are stirred up

explanation.surface: A bold troublemaker can seem muddle-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like an adjective meaning vague, but it is a noun: a knitted garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted buttoned jacket is a woollen garment, informally a woolly.

clue.text: Some people flag and start homeward

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris plant

indicators.note: start means the first letter of homeward

explanation.surface: Some people tire and set off home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a verb meaning tire, but it is the plant, the yellow flag iris.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ireland are a nation, some people among many.

clue.text: Injured man had to carry a gun

indicators.note: to carry says the first piece holds the second

parts.note: he'd is short for he had
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A wounded man had been carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man had' is read as the contraction he'd, and 'to carry' signals that it holds the weapon inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being damaged or hurt means being injured.

clue.text: A measure of length-a matter of feet

definitions.meaning: the basic metric unit of length
the rhythm of verse, counted in metrical feet

explanation.definitionFit: The unit of length is spelt the same as poetic rhythm, which is built from feet.

clue.text: In the evenings octogenarians like a bit of singing

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Old folk enjoy a song at night.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in opera.

clue.text: An elbow-bender turned it over for the musician…

indicators.note: turned says the drinker's word is read backwards

parts.note: an elbow-bender is a heavy drinker, a sot

indicators.note: over says the little word it is flipped round

explanation.surface: A drunk knocked it over for the performer.
explanation.walkthrough: TOSTI is Francesco Paolo Tosti, Italian song composer. 'turned' gives TOS from SOT; 'over' gives TI from IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosti was an Italian composer of popular songs.

clue.text: … finding this somewhat on the slow side

definitions.text: finding this somewhat on the slow side

parts.words: finding this somewhat on the slow side
parts.note: a musical tempo marking meaning rather slow, following on from the composer in the previous clue

explanation.surface: The musician finds this rather slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue follows on from the composer above: this is an Italian tempo marking, a little faster than largo.
explanation.definitionFit: This tempo marking means fairly slow, slightly quicker than largo.

clue.text: What youngsters may play awaiting discovery

definitions.text: What youngsters may play awaiting discovery

parts.words: What youngsters may play awaiting discovery
parts.note: a children's game in which some conceal themselves and wait to be found

explanation.surface: A game children play while waiting to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's game has players concealing themselves until another finds them.
